title: Power Automate: self-healing repairs desktop flow selector failures with AI
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview licensing, captured data and configuration requirements are supported by Microsoft's text. The maker path needs a minor clarification showing how to open the flow before selecting its action; the briefing already reports the conflicting Microsoft descriptions of supported actions.

claims.claim: Self-healing is an AI fallback for UI or web automation failures in Power Automate desktop flows.
claims.quote: Self-healing is an agentic feature that improves the resilience of desktop flows by recovering from UI or web automation failures.

claims.claim: When a selector cannot locate the intended element, AI identifies it and generates an alternative selector.
claims.quote: When an existing selector can no longer locate the intended UI element, Power Automate for desktop uses AI to identify the element and generate an alternative selector.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes self-healing as an agentic feature improving desktop flow resilience.
claims.quote: Self-healing is an agentic feature that improves the resilience of desktop flows

claims.claim: The planned preview includes action-level opt-in for automatic recovery from selector errors.
claims.quote: The preview phase includes an action-level opt-in option for automatically trying to recover from a selector error

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The planned log-only option records a working alternative selector without applying the runtime fix.

claims.fix: Expand controls[2].ui.path and its rendered path to 'My flows > flow > action > Error handling > Self-healing (Preview)'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/flow-designer to sources: it says to open an existing flow from My flows to reach the designer. The existing docs URL supports the control's final steps.
